question: What medical term describes discharge coming out from the ear?
explanation: Otorrhea refers to any fluid discharge originating from the external ear canal. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T3#GNS221_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why do nurses use an otoscope when a patient has ear pain?

options.A: To measure the exact decibel loss of the patient's hearing
options.B: To inspect the ear canal and tympanic membrane for pathology
options.C: To clear impacted earwax before administering oral antibiotics
options.D: To test the function of the vestibulocochlear cranial nerve

explanation: Otoscopy gives direct visual access to check the canal and eardrum for signs of infection or injury causing pain. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T3#GNS221_U2_T3_h1)

question: Which part of the ear canal contains cartilage and wax-producing glands?

options.C: The outer third of the canal

explanation: The cartilaginous outer third of the auditory canal contains hair follicles and glands that produce cerumen. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T3#GNS221_U2_T3_h2)

question: Why is the inner part of the ear canal especially sensitive to pain?

options.A: The cartilage lacks protective subcutaneous tissue
options.B: The skin covering the bony section is very thin
options.C: The tympanic membrane has dense nerve endings
options.D: The cerumen glands press against the temporal bone

explanation: The inner two-thirds of the canal has thin skin resting directly on bone, making it easily irritated by hard instruments. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T3#GNS221_U2_T3_h2)

question: What part of the otoscope controls the brightness of the light?

options.D: The magnifying lens on the head

explanation: The rheostat switch adjusts the brightness of the light bulb during the examination. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T3#GNS221_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is the rule for picking a speculum size for an adult patient?

options.A: Choose the largest speculum that fits comfortably
options.B: Always pick the smallest speculum to avoid any pain
options.C: Use a pediatric speculum for elderly female patients
options.D: Select a medium size regardless of ear canal dimensions

explanation: A larger speculum allows a wider field of view and prevents the tip from inserting too deeply into the canal. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T3#GNS221_U2_T3_h3)

question: How should an adult patient sit for a routine ear exam?

options.A: Standing facing away from the nurse
options.B: Sitting upright with the head tilted away
options.C: Reclining forward with the chin on the chest
options.D: Lying completely flat on the back

explanation: An upright sitting position with the head tilted to the opposite shoulder provides optimal alignment for the examiner. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T3#GNS221_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is the best way to handle a restless toddler during an ear exam?

options.A: Perform the procedure quickly without explaining anything first
options.B: Administer a mild sedative to calm the child down
options.C: Ask the child to lie flat on the floor unassisted
options.D: Have a caregiver hold the child securely against their chest

explanation: Securing the child against a caregiver prevents sudden head movements that could cause the speculum to injure the ear canal. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T3#GNS221_U2_T3_h4)

question: How do you straighten the ear canal of an adult before inserting the speculum?

options.A: Pull the auricle upward and backward
options.B: Pull the auricle straight down and back
options.C: Push the tragus inward over the meatus
options.D: Gently massage the lobe in a circular motion

explanation: Pulling the adult auricle upward and backward straightens the S-shape of the external auditory canal. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T3#GNS221_U2_T3_h5)

question: Why should you rest the back of your hand against the patient's face during otoscopy?

options.A: To warm up the speculum before it touches the skin
options.B: To prevent injury if the patient makes a sudden movement
options.C: To block excess ambient light from entering the ear canal
options.D: To keep your fingers from obscuring the view through the lens

explanation: Anchoring your hand to the patient's face ensures that if they jerk, the otoscope moves with them rather than puncturing the canal. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T3#GNS221_U2_T3_h5)

question: What does a healthy eardrum normally look like?
explanation: A normal, healthy eardrum is translucent and has a pearly-gray color with visible landmarks behind it. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T3#GNS221_U2_T3_h6)

question: Where is the normal cone of light usually seen on a right eardrum?

options.B: At the center of the umbo

explanation: The light reflex shines as a cone in the lower front (anteroinferior) section of the eardrum. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T3#GNS221_U2_T3_h6)

question: Which finding points most clearly to acute middle ear infection (otitis media)?

options.A: A clear amber fluid level behind a retracted eardrum
options.C: A pearly-gray membrane with a visible light cone
options.D: Dry, flaky skin lining an empty auditory canal

explanation: Acute otitis media causes inflammation and pus buildup, resulting in a red, bulging eardrum. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T3#GNS221_U2_T3_h7)

question: What usually blocks the view of the eardrum during an ear exam?
explanation: A complete blockage of the ear canal by hardened earwax prevents light from reaching the eardrum. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T3#GNS221_U2_T3_h7)

question: When should you avoid doing an otoscopic exam for safety reasons?

options.A: When head trauma with clear fluid leakage is suspected
options.B: When there is visible yellow earwax in the canal
options.D: When the patient complains of mild, dull ear pain

explanation: Inserting an instrument into the ear during a suspected skull fracture can introduce pathogens into the cranial cavity. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T3#GNS221_U2_T3_h8)

question: Which of these is an unsafe infection control practice for otoscope specula?

options.A: Discarding single-use plastic specula immediately after examination
options.B: Cleaning reusable specula thoroughly before high-level disinfection
options.C: Subjecting reusable metal specula to proper sterilization
options.D: Wiping a disposable speculum with a dry tissue and reusing it

explanation: Disposable specula are meant for single use only and must never be reused between patients regardless of cleaning. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T3#GNS221_U2_T3_h8)
